title: Connect a desktop app
description: An app on this computer is asking for access to your {appName} account. Nothing is issued until you approve it here.

permissions.heading: If you approve, this app will be able to:
permissions.upload: Upload files to your library. They appear as yours.
permissions.read: See your account details, storage limit and folders.
permissions.links: Create short links under your tag, and save its own settings to your account.
permissions.notIncluded: It never sees your password or your two-factor codes, and it cannot change your sign-in details or turn two-factor off. You can revoke its access at any time under Integrations.

local: The key goes straight to {host} on this computer and nowhere else.
unexpected: If you did not just start this app yourself, close this page. Nothing has been issued yet.

done.title: {client} is connected
done.body: The app now has its own key to your {appName} account.

denied.title: Nothing was issued
denied.body: No key was created, and the app was told you declined.

refused.title: Could not connect the app
refused.signed-out: Your session ended. Sign in again, then reopen the link from the app.
refused.invalid-request: This request is incomplete or malformed. Start the sign-in from the app again.
refused.rate-limited: Too many keys were issued from here in a short time. Wait a few minutes and try again.
refused.error: Something went wrong while creating the key. Try again in a moment.

manual.title: The app did not answer on {host}
manual.body: The key was created, but {client} could not be reached. It may have stopped waiting. Copy the key below and paste it into the app, or make sure the app is still open and send it again.
manual.hint: Treat this key like a password. Anyone holding it can upload and delete files on your account.
manual.retry: Send it to the app again

invalid.title: This link is not a valid request
invalid.description: It is missing something an app has to send, or it was altered on the way here.
invalid.body: Start the sign-in from inside the desktop app, so it can supply its own port and one-time code. If you were not expecting this page, you can simply close it.
